Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

entry = rlm.harness.create_memory(title='ARC task-bd7055f7: reconstruct motif layout and mark tile coordinates', id='arc_task_bd7055f7_reconstruct_motif_layout_mark_coordinates', content='For ARC task-bd7055f7, repeated 2-colored motifs occupy regularly spaced tiles (often tile pitch 5 with 4x4 motif cells); color 3 marks a hidden tile row/column/region. Read the motif P from a copy, using the full tile anchor including any leading/trailing zero cells. Its 2/0 pixel mask also gives the large-scale occupancy pattern of motif copies. Clear the 3 region to 0 and, within it, add a full copy of P at each tile coordinate (r,c) where P[r][c] is 2; elsewhere leave the tile blank. For every motif copy (including newly inserted copies) at macro tile coordinate (r,c), recolor its local pixel P[r][c] from 2 to 8. Preserve all other cells. Demos: 3x3 P=110/101/010 with masked last column adds only macro tile (1,2); P=101/010/110 with masked last column adds none; 4x4 P=0111/0100/1110/1100 with masked second row adds macro tile (1,1). Important: anchor motifs to the regular tile grid, not the visible nonzero bounding box: leading zeros are part of the tile, and every existing copy needs its coordinate marker (first attempt missed an existing copy’s mark).', global_=True)
print(entry)
